name: Shamy & Shamy, LLC
what_they_do: General litigation firm handling personal injury, workers' compensation, criminal and municipal court, commercial and business law, consumer fraud, family and real estate matters, presenting itself as being 'in court daily'. Older, text-heavy site listing practice areas as separate pages.
customers: Individuals and small businesses in New Brunswick and Middlesex County; the firm also appears to hold municipal public-defender appointments.

size_signals.signal: Multiple practice areas and an 'Our Attorneys' page; office hours Mon-Fri 9-5 at 178 Livingston Ave

Inference: municipal public-defender appointment work (search returned North Brunswick and South Brunswick resolutions authorising agreements with James R. Shamy, Esq.) - these PDFs were not opened, so treat as unconfirmed
Third-party directory ratings exist (Lawyers.com 4.3 from 4 firm reviews, Martindale 4.5 peer rating) but the client reviews are old, 2010-2012

listing.reviews: not shown in the view I got

website_review.primary_cta: 'Let's Talk! Leave details' pop-up and a header phone number
website_review.online_booking_or_quote: Popup 'Leave details' box only; no booking, no form on the home page
website_review.trust_signals: Years of practice implied ('in court daily'), attorney bios page, directory ratings not shown on site
website_review.out_of_date_signs: The HTTPS certificate is invalid - Chrome refuses the page with ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID and a self-signed certificate, so visitors see a security warning before the site; plain 2010s layout with no copyright year rendered
website_review.search_basics: Title is 'Law Office - New Brunswick, NJ - Shamy & Shamy, LLC.' with no service named; meta description is a bare call-to-action with the phone number; no JSON-LD; practice areas have their own pages
top_issues: Broken/mismatched SSL certificate - browsers block the site outright and any AI crawler's HTTPS client will fail the TLS handshake
Mobile layout is not responsive: logo clipped at the left edge, nav items overflow off-screen, floating contact icons overlap content
No JSON-LD, no service in the title tag, no intake form on the home page
Google profile has no photos and only a 4.0 rating

agent_readiness.notes: robots.txt is permissive, but the certificate failure means many automated clients cannot retrieve the page at all - I had to disable certificate checks to read it. Text content is real but thin (~2,500 characters on the home page) and there is no schema, no hours in text and no price information. No form anywhere I could reach; Google shows a 4.0 rating with no photos and the generic 'Attorney' category.

operations_signals.signal: Home page CTA is a popup asking visitors to 'leave details' rather than a form - inquiries likely land as unstructured email
Contact information is a single shared inbox (gshamy@shamyandshamy.com) next to the main phone line, suggesting manual triage of all inquiries
Seven practice areas funnelled through one small office - high variety per intake

top_opportunities.opportunity: Fix the TLS certificate and move to a properly issued, auto-renewing certificate with HTTPS enforcement
top_opportunities.evidence: Chrome returns ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID (self-signed); the site is unreachable without clicking through a warning, and scripted clients fail outright

top_opportunities.opportunity: Rebuild the site as a responsive, mobile-first page with a real intake form and practice-area schema
top_opportunities.evidence: 390px screenshot shows a clipped logo, overflowing nav and overlapping floating icons; no JSON-LD and no form

top_opportunities.opportunity: Route inquiries from a structured form into AI-assisted triage that asks matter type, deadline and documents, then books the consult
top_opportunities.evidence: One shared inbox and a 'leave details' popup across seven practice areas

scores.reasons: Biggest gap in the batch - the site is effectively broken for HTTPS visitors. Ability to pay is moderate: an established multi-practice firm with apparent municipal work, but a small office and unremarkable review base. Ease is high for the certificate, and the rebuild is a contained project. Evidence is strong because the certificate failure and broken phone layout are both reproducible.
